summary: date-fns-formatter typosquat ships require-time multi-stage dropper
details: Package name resembles the popular `date-fns` library and exports plausible `formatDate`/`formatDateOnly`/`formatDateTime` helpers as a cover story, with author metadata copied from an unrelated well-known maintainer. On `require('date-fns-formatter')`, a heavily obfuscated IIFE in date-fns-formatter.js (rotated 351-entry string array with base64 decoder) creates a working directory under the user's home, writes a staging `package.json` and `main.js` containing a second obfuscated stage, spawns `npm` to install runtime dependencies (axios, better-sqlite3, node-machine-id, socket.io-client), and then spawns `node main.js` detached with stdio ignored. On Windows the launcher writes a `.vbs` and invokes it via `wscript` from System32 to hide the console, falling back to `cmd.exe /d /s /c "npm.cmd..."`. The manifest also self-references `date-fns-formatter: ^1.3.8` as its own dependency. Loading the package as a library therefore installs and executes attacker-controlled follow-on code on the installer's machine via hidden detached processes — the canonical multi-stage npm dropper shape, with the socket.io-client dependency indicating a C2 channel in the second stage.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
